knowledge_point.title: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix

question.:question/problem:
$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix},\,B=\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 0 & -5 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form $R_{i}:=R_{i}+kR_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above $a_{32}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{1}:=R_{1}-2R_{3}}\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 0 & -5 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{2}:=R_{2}-2R_{3}}\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 0 & -5 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}=B
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$R_{1}:=R_{1}-2R_{3}$ and $R_{2}:=R_{2}-2R_{3}$.

question.:question/problem:
$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}3 & -6 & -8 \\ -1 & 9 & 8 \\ -8 & -2 & -1\end{bmatrix},\,B=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 21 & 16 \\ -1 & 9 & 8 \\ 0 & -74 & -65\end{bmatrix}
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form $R_{i}:=R_{i}+kR_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above and below $a_{21}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}3 & -6 & -8 \\ -1 & 9 & 8 \\ -8 & -2 & -1\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{1}:=R_{1}+3R_{2}}\begin{bmatrix}0 & 21 & 16 \\ -1 & 9 & 8 \\ -8 & -2 & -1\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{3}:=R_{3}-8R_{2}}\begin{bmatrix}0 & 21 & 16 \\ -1 & 9 & 8 \\ 0 & -74 & -65\end{bmatrix}=B
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$R_{1}:=R_{1}+3R_{2}$ and $R_{3}:=R_{3}-8R_{2}$.

question.:question/problem:
$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & -5 & -8 \\ -1 & -5 & 6\end{bmatrix},\,B=\begin{bmatrix}0 & -12 & 14 \\ 0 & -10 & -2 \\ -1 & -5 & 6\end{bmatrix}
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form $R_{i}:=R_{i}+kR_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above $a_{31}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}2 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & -5 & -8 \\ -1 & -5 & 6\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{1}:=R_{1}+2R_{3}}\begin{bmatrix}0 & -12 & 14 \\ 1 & -5 & -8 \\ -1 & -5 & 6\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{2}:=R_{2}+R_{3}}\begin{bmatrix}0 & -12 & 14 \\ 0 & -10 & -2 \\ -1 & -5 & 6\end{bmatrix}=B
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$R_{1}:=R_{1}+2R_{3}$ and $R_{2}:=R_{2}+R_{3}$.

A=\begin{bmatrix}-7 & -3 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 6 & 12 & 12\end{bmatrix},\,B=\begin{bmatrix}0 & -10 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 18 & 12\end{bmatrix}
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form $R_{i}:=R_{i}+kR_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above and below $a_{21}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}-7 & -3 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 6 & 12 & 12\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{1}:=R_{1}-7R_{2}}\begin{bmatrix}0 & -10 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 6 & 12 & 12\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{3}:=R_{3}+6R_{2}}\begin{bmatrix}0 & -10 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 18 & 12\end{bmatrix}=B
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$R_{1}:=R_{1}-7R_{2}$ and $R_{3}:=R_{3}+6R_{2}$.
